Haken.et:
From Middle High German hāke, from Old High German hāggo, hācko, hāko, from Proto-West Germanic *hākō, from Proto-Germanic *hēkô (see *hakô), from Proto-Indo-European *keg-, *keng- (“peg; hook”). Cognate with Old English hǣca (“hook, bolt”).

generic term for a diacritic mark, e.g. a háček, cedilla, etc.
Häkchen.et: From Haken (“hook”) + -chen (diminutive suffix). Compare Dutch haakje, Czech háček.

s: to tease, to chaff, to banter
generic term for a diacritic mark, e.g. a hacek, cedilla, etc.

Hakensaugwurm.et: From Haken (“hook”) + saugen (“to suck”) + Wurm (“worm”), literally “hooksucking worm”.
